root_cause_finding.summary: The off arm's `skill-repo:` source-qualifier isolation (PR #3185's central guarantee: 'no skills root at all for the off arm, no stub to misclassify') does not actually block skill content delivery. `skills.py::_skill_repo_root()`'s resolution order is: MUSTER_SKILL_REPO env (if set AND is_dir()) -> sibling clone -> `_skill_repo_managed_root()` (a shared, repo-owned, always-populated clone at `<this orchestrator's checkout>/runs/rulebooks/skill-repository/skills/`). When MUSTER_SKILL_REPO is explicitly set but points at a path that does not exist (prepare_arms.py's whole off-arm strategy), the `is_dir()` check fails and the function silently FALLS THROUGH to the next tier instead of returning None -- treating 'explicitly set to an intentionally-absent path' identically to 'never set at all'. The off arm's dispatch therefore resolved the pinned skill from the shared managed clone, completely bypassing the isolated-HOME/env-var trust root.
evidence: manifest.json: off arm's skills_root = /tmp/consumer-path-off-skills-absent-834a4827a73b48b0af99f5600a0873d4, confirmed not present on disk (os.path.exists == False).

/home/jwjung/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/tokenmaxxxer/skills.py:197-211 (_skill_repo_root()): env tier returns the resolved path only `if p.is_dir()`; on failure, control falls through to the sibling-clone and managed-clone tiers rather than returning None -- confirmed by reading the function body directly this session.

off arm's SECOND Skill call this same session, for an unrelated/unmounted skill name ('hypothesis-testing'), correctly failed with 'Unknown skill: hypothesis-testing' -- proving the managed-clone fallback only serves skills that are actually present in that shared clone, not an unconditional pass-through; the pinned target skill happens to be present there because every session on this machine bootstraps that same managed clone at SessionStart.
root_cause_finding.severity: This affects every consumer-path off-arm dispatch that has ever run or will run under the current `_skill_repo_root()` fallback chain, not just this pair -- it explains why H1 has never passed in four rounds of this issue once it became possible to observe it (rounds 1-3 never got a session log for both arms at all; this is the first round that did). Any prior H2 'off arm' result anywhere in this project's history that relied on `skill-repo:<absent-path>` isolation should be treated as unverified for this specific guarantee.
root_cause_finding.resolution_path: Not fixed this round -- this is a defect in shared, core infrastructure (skills.py, used by every `--skills skill-repo:` dispatch across the whole repo, not scoped to docs/issue-3245's consumer-path scripts) and warrants its own dedicated issue with its own review, not a same-PR patch bundled into a measurement round. The fix shape: `_skill_repo_root()` should distinguish 'MUSTER_SKILL_REPO unset' from 'MUSTER_SKILL_REPO set but invalid' and fail closed (return None, or raise) on the latter, never silently falling through to a shared managed clone that defeats the whole point of an explicit absent-path override.
